passage:
Santosh, nine, watched Dada take a long time to cross the living room of their Lucknow flat, leaning on his stick. Then Dada asked, "Who won the match?" He had asked that ten minutes ago.
Santosh went to the kitchen. "Papa, is Dada very sick?" he whispered.
Deepak dried his hands. "Dada's body is old now, beta. His legs are weaker and sometimes he forgets things. It's not his fault. He's still our Dada."
"Is he scared?"
"Sometimes, I think. That's why we're gentle."
Santosh went back and sat on the floor by Dada's chair. "Dada, shall I read you the cricket page?" Dada smiled and patted his head. Santosh read slowly, and when Dada asked about the match again, he just read the score once more.

qa.q: What did Santosh offer to read to Dada?
qa.a: He offered to read Dada the cricket page.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling when he whispered to Papa in the kitchen?
qa.a: He was worried and a little frightened that Dada was very sick.

qa.q: What helped Santosh know how to act around Dada?
qa.a: Deepak's honest, simple explanation, and then doing something together like reading the cricket page.

qa.q: How might Dada feel when Santosh sits by his chair and reads to him?
qa.a: Dada probably feels loved and less alone, which shows when he smiles and pats Santosh's head.

grounding: It shows a child seeing a grandparent move slowly and repeat questions, and learning respect and tenderness through an honest explanation and a shared activity.

passage:
"Bhaiya, why does Nani need help to get up now?" Aditi whispered on the verandah.
Nitin looked over. Nani was gripping the chair arm, trying to stand. "Her knees are old and tired. Like when you've run all day, but always."
"And she asked my name twice today."
"Sometimes she forgets. It's part of getting old for her. It doesn't mean she loves you less."
Aditi chewed her lip. "Will she forget me?"
"I don't know. But she remembers how to shell peas better than anyone."
They went over. "Nani, can we help with the peas?" Nitin asked.
Nani's face lit up. "Come, come. Aditi, you split the pods like this."
Aditi sat close. When Nani's hands shook, Aditi held the bowl steady.

qa.q: What did the children help Nani with?
qa.a: They helped Nani with the peas, splitting the pods.

qa.q: What was Aditi afraid of?
qa.a: She was afraid that Nani would forget her one day.

qa.q: How did Nitin help Aditi understand Nani?
qa.a: He gave her simple, honest explanations about Nani's tired knees and forgetting, then found something they could all do together.

qa.q: How might Nani feel when the children ask to help with the peas?
qa.a: Nani likely feels happy and useful, as her face lights up and she shows Aditi how to split the pods.

grounding: It shows a child noticing a grandmother who needs help and repeats things, and learning tenderness through honest answers and a shared task.

passage: When I was ten, Nana came to live with us, and at first he scared me a little. He walked so slowly, holding the wall, and he told me the same story about the train to Lahore three times in one day. Once he called me by my uncle's name. I'm Vaibhav, and I remember hiding in my room because I didn't know what to say. My cousin Avni laughed at him behind his back, and I felt bad but laughed too. Then Mummy sat with me. 'Nana's body and memory are getting old and tired. He's still Nana inside.' She suggested I do a jigsaw puzzle with him. I did. He was slow, but he found every edge piece, and he told me about the Lahore train again. This time I listened properly. It was actually a good story.

qa.q: What story did Nana tell three times in one day?
qa.a: The story about the train to Lahore.

qa.q: How did Vaibhav feel when Nana first came to live with them?
qa.a: Vaibhav felt a little scared and unsure, hiding away without knowing what to say.

qa.q: What helped Vaibhav connect with Nana?
qa.a: Mummy's simple honest explanation and doing a jigsaw puzzle together.

qa.q: How might Nana have felt when the children laughed behind his back?
qa.a: He may have noticed and felt hurt or embarrassed, even if he said nothing.

grounding: Shows a child seeing a grandparent move slowly and repeat stories, feeling scared, and learning respect and love through a simple explanation and a shared activity.

passage:
Note to Dhruv's parents, Class 4
Today in creative writing, Dhruv wrote a story about a grandmother who 'walks with a stick and forgets the kettle on'. He added, 'The boy is scared she will fall and die.' At break he asked me quietly whether old people's legs stop working. I think he is worried about his Dadi. I told him simply that as people get older their bodies slow down and sometimes need more help, and that it's normal to feel scared and to love them at the same time. He seemed relieved to talk. You might find a shared job he can do with Dadi, like watering plants or reading together, so he feels close rather than frightened. Happy to talk more.
Rukmini, class teacher

qa.q: What did Dhruv write that the grandmother walks with?
qa.a: A stick.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling about his Dadi?
qa.a: He was scared that she would fall and die, and worried about her getting older.

qa.q: What did Rukmini suggest the family could do?
qa.a: Find a shared job for Dhruv and Dadi, like watering plants or reading together.

qa.q: How might Dadi feel doing a shared job with Dhruv?
qa.a: She would likely feel loved and valued, glad to spend time with her grandson.

grounding: Shows a teacher noticing a child frightened by a frail grandparent, and offering an honest simple explanation and shared activities to build tenderness and respect.

passage:
Saturday
Today Bidisha Nani couldn't get up the stairs by herself. Mummy had to hold her arm and they went one step at a time. Nani's hand was shaking. I got scared and ran to my room. Later Mummy came and said Nani's knees are old and tired, like a bicycle that needs oiling, and she's not going anywhere. Then I felt bad for running away. So in the evening I sat with Nani on the veranda and helped her shell peas. She showed me how to pop them out with my thumb. She laughed when one flew into my hair. Her hands were slow, but she still knew the best way. I think I'll help her with the peas every Saturday.
Nazia

qa.q: What did Nazia help Nani do on the veranda?
qa.a: Shell peas.

qa.q: How did Nazia feel when Nani couldn't climb the stairs?
qa.a: Nazia felt scared, and later felt bad about running away.

qa.q: What turned Nazia's fear into closeness?
qa.a: Mummy's simple explanation about Nani's tired knees and sharing the pea-shelling together.

qa.q: How might Nani feel when Nazia helps with the peas?
qa.a: Nani probably feels happy and loved, laughing and enjoying teaching Nazia.

grounding: Shows a child seeing a grandparent needing help, feeling frightened then tender, and learning love and respect through explanation and a shared task.

passage: Every summer Simran stayed at Nani's house in Nabha, and every summer Nani, Avni, had raced her to the mango tree. This year Nani took the three steps to the courtyard one at a time, holding the wall, and asked twice at lunch whether Simran had eaten. Simran went quiet and hid behind the cowshed door. That evening Mummy found her there. "Nani's body is getting old, beta. Her knees hurt and sometimes she forgets things. She is still Nani." The next morning Simran carried a stool to the courtyard and asked Nani to teach her the old phulkari stitch. Nani's fingers were slow but sure. They sewed until the shadows moved, and Nani laughed at Simran's crooked petals.

qa.q: What did Simran ask Nani to teach her?
qa.a: The old phulkari stitch.

qa.q: Why did Simran hide behind the cowshed door?
qa.a: She felt frightened and confused seeing Nani move slowly and repeat questions, so unlike the Nani who used to race her.

qa.q: What helped Simran feel close to Nani again?
qa.a: Mummy's honest, simple explanation, and a shared activity where Nani could still teach her something.

qa.q: How might Nani have felt sewing with Simran?
qa.a: She probably felt happy and valued, laughing at the crooked petals while passing on a skill.

grounding: Shows a child noticing a grandparent moving slowly and repeating herself, feeling frightened, and an honest explanation plus a shared activity bringing tenderness and respect.
